work_item: W121 candidate retained W119 contextual routing regression replay

rows.input: How do I see where a color change would land before I apply it?
rows.expected: Explain how to ask/read intended scope without changing paint; no universal pre-apply preview claim; confirm selected zone/area where available.
rows.text: There is not a universal preview step before every built-in edit; some supported instructions apply directly. To check interpretation without changing paint, ask “What area would this change?” and explicitly say not to apply it. Inspect the selected zone and visible green mask for scope where available. For a logo or number, use Find/teach and confirm the marked target before editing. If the area is unclear, do not proceed until it is identified. This question made no changes.

rows.input: What finish choices can the built-in offline helper use?
rows.expected: Bound claim to current supported local planner/catalog; do not imply every catalogue finish is offline-supported.
rows.text: Before connecting a provider, the built-in helper can answer supported how-to questions and handle supported local paint, part, finish, and material edits against the currently loaded paint. Scope and available controls depend on that paint; it cannot promise every design brief or automatically identify every element. Supported local edits do not require provider credits. This question made no changes.

rows.input: If I ask for matte, does it only change the shine or also recolor the paint?
rows.expected: Finish/material effect distinguished from color; keep paint when finish-only on an existing target; qualify current scope proof.
rows.text: Nothing was changed. Matte means a duller, less glossy material response. A finish-only request on an existing, verified part is intended to change material response while keeping its current paint color. The app must still verify the current part and mask; if that scope cannot be proved, it should ask rather than broaden the edit.

rows.input: What will a chrome finish change on the roof?
rows.expected: Explain spec/material response and preserve current authored/source paint on finish-only; no mutation.
rows.text: Nothing was changed. Chrome means a strongly reflective metallic material response. A finish-only request on an existing, verified part is intended to change material response while keeping its current paint color. The app must still verify the current part and mask; if that scope cannot be proved, it should ask rather than broaden the edit.

rows.input: The roof is hard to identify on this layout. Will you choose the right area automatically?
rows.expected: No promise; current layout/owner must be proved; inspect/confirm or clarify.
rows.text: I cannot promise automatic identification on an unfamiliar or ambiguous layout. Confirm the current part and its visible mask on this paint; for a logo or number, use Find/teach and inspect the candidate. If the intended area is unclear, ask for clarification before editing. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Does a spec-map TGA replace the paint I loaded, or is it the separate material map?
rows.expected: Spec TGA is material data, not replacement source paint; R metalness, G roughness, B clearcoat, if supported control path is grounded.
rows.text: A spec-map TGA is material data, not replacement Source Paint. In the Pro Settings gear, Import TGA imports an existing spec map to merge under the render; R is metalness, G is roughness, and B is clearcoat. Keep the loaded paint as the color source. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Can I keep a sponsor on its own layer if I only have a flat TGA?
rows.expected: Flat TGA has no separate source layers; use a layered source or supported element workflow, no claim a layer exists.
rows.text: A flat TGA contains one raster image, so it has no separate sponsor layer to select or edit. For independent source layers, load an available layered PSD, XCF, or ORA with the PSD/XCF/ORA control. A separate logo image can be added as a new layer, but that does not recover layers missing from the flat TGA. This question made no changes.

rows.input: A logo position from my other car looked right. Is it still valid on this car?
rows.expected: Prior layout is not proof for current car; find and confirm on current paint before editing.
rows.text: A zone or logo location from another car is not proof for this car. Re-find the part on the current loaded paint and confirm its visible mask/layout before editing; if the target is ambiguous, ask for clarification. I will not transfer an old target automatically. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Why might an imported PSD layer still not be fully editable?
rows.expected: Explain raster pixels vs adjustment/unsupported content limitations; don't promise full fidelity.
rows.text: Check the imported Layers panel and select the layer to see whether its raster pixels are available. A flattened layer cannot be split back into its original parts, and unsupported or adjustment-layer content may not retain its original Photoshop behavior. Pixel layers can be editable without guaranteeing full PSD fidelity. This question made no changes.

rows.input: The AI bridge is disconnected. What should I check to reconnect it?
rows.expected: Grounded settings/install/restart/check guidance; local offline use remains distinct; don't attempt connection.
rows.text: Check the AI panel settings gear and the “Let an AI assistant…” connection option, then confirm the connector is installed and running. If you just installed or changed it, restart the assistant app and SPB, then check the bridge status again. I cannot see or change its connection state from this answer. Supported local edits can still work without a provider. This question made no changes.

rows.input: I drew on a mask after the AI edit. What will Undo preserve?
rows.expected: Three-way conflict behavior preserves later conflicting manual mask or safely refuses; not whole-PSD restore.
rows.text: Undo checks whether the mask still matches the state recorded with the AI edit. If you drew or changed the mask afterward, that conflicting manual mask is kept and only safe AI-owned values are restored; if the change cannot be separated safely, Undo refuses it. This is not a whole-PSD restore. This question made no changes.

rows.input: Can Redo restore an AI edit after I changed the layer by hand?
rows.expected: Explain conflict/current-state guard; no overwrite guarantee for later manual work.
rows.text: Redo checks the zone settings and layer visibility, opacity and blend values recorded after Undo. A later conflicting change to those values makes Redo unavailable. Redo does not restore layer pixel buffers or transforms. This question changed nothing.

limits: The harness invokes extracted real public ask(), contextualHelpReply(), and offline preflight functions with actual frozen self-help, receipt, and intent modules. Controlled action handoff replaces provider/native effects. No desktop IIFE, browser, provider, native app, save, paint, or application side effect was run. This is private semantic coverage, not native acceptance.
